title: The 10 Best Cordless Die Grinders
subtitle: Battery-powered straight and right-angle die grinders for grinding, porting and weld cleanup, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless die grinder spins small bits and wheels fast for grinding, porting and deburring, without the air hose. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a brushless motor, speed control, batteries in the box and a brake).

changelog.note: Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on every listing. Biggest price moves: the VERVEWAVE WT8801-01 dropped from $36.09 to $29.99; the Makita XDG01Z dropped from $233.49 to $197.
Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Brushless Variable Speed Die Grinder, Tool Only (DCG426B)
products.verdict: The most-reviewed and best-rated cordless die grinder here: brushless, up to 25,000 RPM with a variable trigger, and LEDs at the nose.
products.best_for: DEWALT owners porting, deburring and cleaning welds.
products.skip_if: You need a right-angle head for tight spots.

products.name: Milwaukee M12 FUEL 1/4" Straight Die Grinder, Tool Only (2486-20)

specs.extras: 0.3 HP; Milwaukee says it outperforms pneumatic by 20%

products.verdict: A compact M12 FUEL die grinder that Milwaukee pitches as a replacement for air die grinders, with 4-mode speed control.
products.best_for: Mechanics replacing an air die grinder with something cordless.
products.skip_if: You need 18V power for heavy grinding.

products.name: Milwaukee M12 FUEL 1/4" Right Angle Die Grinder Kit with 2 Batteries (3485-22)

products.best_for: Starting on M12 with a straight die grinder.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL Braking Die Grinder, Slide Switch (2939-20)

products.best_for: Users who prefer a slide switch over a paddle.
products.skip_if: You want the best-rated model; this one is 3.8 stars.
pros: Up to 12 in of weld bead per charge (claimed)

products.name: Makita XDG01Z 18V LXT 1/4" Die Grinder, Tool Only
products.verdict: Makita's 18V LXT die grinder with a slim barrel grip and slide switch, for Makita owners.

products.name: SEESII 1/4" Brushless Right Angle Die Grinder Kit with 2 Batteries and 23 Accessories (DG21 Pro)
products.verdict: A budget right-angle kit with a brushless motor, two batteries and 23 accessories, for a fraction of Milwaukee's kit price.
products.best_for: Occasional users who want a right-angle grinder cheaply.

products.name: VERVEWAVE Cordless Die Grinder for DEWALT 20V MAX Battery, Up to 26,000 RPM (WT8801-01)
products.verdict: A cheap DEWALT-battery die grinder with a carbide bit, for occasional grinding.
products.best_for: DEWALT owners who grind once in a while.
products.skip_if: You use a die grinder often; the DCG426B is far better proven.

avoid.name: 1100W Brushless Braking Die Grinder Compatible with Milwaukee Battery, 3 Level Variable Speed Up to 26000RPM
avoid.verdict: A Milwaukee-battery clone whose 1,100 W claim would need more current than an 18V pack is built to deliver.
reasons: 1,100 W at 18V is about 61 amps, far beyond what a compact power tool battery delivers continuously. Milwaukee rates its own M12 FUEL grinders at 0.3 to 0.4 HP (about 220 to 300 W).
It's rated 3.8 stars, the lowest of the die grinders we looked at except Milwaukee's slide-switch model.
Milwaukee's own M18 FUEL 2984-20 adds a real brake, five speeds and Milwaukee's warranty.

buyers_guide.q: What is a die grinder for?
buyers_guide.a: Grinding, porting, deburring, cleaning welds and cutting with small bits and wheels on a 1/4-inch shank. Think of it as a heavy-duty rotary tool.
Straight die grinders reach into holes and pipes. Right-angle grinders get into tight engine bays and corners where a straight body won't fit.
Air die grinders need a big compressor running constantly. Cordless models like Milwaukee's M12 FUEL are built to replace them for most shop work, without a hose.
A brake stops the bit quickly when you release the switch, so you can set the tool down sooner and it's less likely to grab.
Up to 25,000 RPM is typical. Lower speeds suit larger wheels and softer metals; variable speed lets you match the bit.
